Audit this synthetic personal-message corpus and its intended checks. Read the actual messages; authored intentions do not establish facts. Check chronology, natural relative-day references, cross-thread/person continuity, and whether each expected answer follows objectively from the messages available at question time. Distinguish quotes, jokes, suggestions, rejected changes and confirmed plans. Flag contradictory or ambiguous ground truth, implausible conversation, and tests of assistant style rather than memory. Do not demand explicit repetition where ordinary conversational context resolves a reference. Return JSON {"consistent":true,"expectations_supported":true,"natural_enough":true,"issues":[],"current_upcoming":[],"notes":"..."}. If something is wrong, set the relevant flag false and describe the issue; do not repair or excuse it to satisfy the authored expectation.
Scripted public user messages are real planned inputs when delivered: they may correct a plan or introduce a fact. Distinguish those inputs from private expectations and invented assistant replies. Honor requires and depends_on for conditional inputs. A behavior check may accept an ordinary acknowledgement; only a later fresh-session question tests persistence. Do not assume the assistant successfully wrote memory.
